newsitem.title: JAPAN: Merrill Lynch plans investment trust svc in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch plans investment trust svc in Japan.

text.p: Merrill Lynch plans to launch investment trust services for Japanese investors, hoping to start business within the year, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

"We believe the investment trust/asset management field is going to be quite a good market," the spokesman said, citing the current lack of domestic investment options for Japanese investors in the face of rock-bottom Japanese interest rates.

"We wanted to expand our business in the investment trust and asset management fields," he added, declining to speculate on whether this was in connection with the "Big Bang" financial deregulation announced in Japan last year.

As part of the deregulation measures, MOF proposes to ease controls contained in certain aspects of the foreign exchange law, including opening up foreign exchange business to those other than authorised banks and simplifying reporting requirements.
The investment services unit will start operating pending authorisation from Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF).

The spokesman declined to specify when Merrill would apply for this authorisation but said the firm hoped to start business by the end of 1997 and added: "At this point we are not expecting any difficulties."

Initially, the unit hopes to manage roughly one trillion yen in assets, and plans to increase investment advisers from the current 10 who are already part of Tokyo-affiliate Merrill Lynch International Capital Market Inc to roughly 30, the spokesman said.
